items.rationale: The window is thrown away when a session ends and the model keeps nothing on its own, so only something the program wrote down outside the window can carry the booking into the new chat. Picking a or b shows the belief that the model remembers earlier chats.

Call 1 reads 1,500. Call 2 reads 1,500 + 20 + 80 = 1,600. Call 3 reads 1,600 + 20 + 80 = 1,700. The total is 1,500 + 1,600 + 1,700 = 4,800. An answer of 1,700 counts only the last call and forgets that every call re-sends the history.

360,000 tokens is well above the size that fits comfortably in a prompt, and it is only needed occasionally, so it is indexed and searched, with only the best chunks pulled in. Pasting it in (a) would re-read it on every call.

items.answer: Old results still clutter the window and are re-read on every call, so cost and the chance of missing the important part stay high at any window size.
accepted: Windows of every size get cluttered with old results, which still cost tokens on every call
The model recalls the contents less accurately as the window fills, however big it is
Old results still get re-sent each call so cost grows
A bigger window still fills with irrelevant old results and the model gets worse at finding the useful part
items.rationale: Any one valid reason is enough: clutter and context rot happen at every window size, and every call re-reads the old results, so cost grows. An answer that says only 'bigger windows are expensive' without the re-reading or clutter point is partial.

A chunk that does not say where it came from is easy to miss. Adding a line that names the machine and manual before indexing lets the search match it. Moving all chunks into the system prompt (b) throws away the point of retrieval.
